newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy buys 630 bln lire floating rate certificates.
newsitem.headline: Italy buys 630 bln lire floating rate certificates.

text.p: The Italian Treasury said it had bought back floating rate certificates (CCTs) with a total nominal value of 630 billion lire on December 31, 1996.
A Treasury statement said it used its sinking fund for the purchase using 653 billion lire, which corresponded to the market value of the certificates plus respective daily interest rates.
It said the CCTs, which had been bought back were 330 billion lire of March 1, 1993-2000 CCTs and 300 billion lire of June 1, 1992-99 CCTs.
